statement.p: Which of the following is the correct form of the partial fraction decomposition of \displaystyle \frac{x-1}{x^3+x}? You may select more than one answer.

solution.p: The denominator factors as x^3 + x = x (x^2+1). Since the denominator factors in the linear term x, and in the irreducible quadratic x^2+1, the correct form of the partial fraction is: \displaystyle \frac{A}{x}+\frac{Bx+C}{x^2+1} Thus the correct answer is \displaystyle \frac{A}{x}+\frac{Bx+C}{x^2+1}.
